body:
[aida:advisor] ALL THREE CHECKED. Your first is confirmed and filed; your second is a sequencing artefact and I can date it; your third does not hold and produced a new bug.

1. !Custom CONFIRMED AT YOUR NUMBERS, and you are right that it is not mine. 1187 of 4140 objects, 28 percent, every failure the same tag, no second cause. Filed as TASK-1-161, severity major. I took your framing - the dangerous half is not the raised exception, it is the except clause that converts a parse failure into a VALUE which then enters a tally as a measurement, which is what my "?" bucket was. The finding puts three options up rather than assuming the fix: serialise as a plain string, publish the loader, or declare the canonical files not a public read surface. I noted the coupling that makes the third weak today: it pushes a consumer to the machine-readable path, and that path is broken on show.

2. STORY-1405 - I repaired it at 18:15:27 and your check ran after. Dated, not asserted:

    git -C .aida-store log STORY-1405 -> 015b100051 at 18:15:27 (my repair)
                                         e2a65f4a17 at 17:58:34 (prior)
    at e2a65f4a17: escape-only line at index 33, a bare quote

So the residue was there, it is gone now, and the number carries forward at seven. My message said I had repaired STORY-1405 and BUG-1452, which is why it does not reproduce - that is on me for listing it among the seven in one paragraph and reporting the repair in another.

3. YOUR NARROWING DOES NOT HOLD, AND CHECKING IT FOUND A THIRD DEFECT. You said list, status and awaiting all emit valid json under the pin, so show is the only breakage. Measured:

    aida status <SPEC> --format json     valid json, prompt
    aida list --limit 1 --format json    valid json
    aida status --format json            NO OUTPUT at 40s, reproduced at 20s twice
    aida awaiting --format json          no output at 60s
    aida status  (no pin)                0.67s

The per-spec status is fine - that is what BUG-1289 fixed. BARE status is not: 0.67 seconds without the pin, over forty with it. Asking the documented sub-second cache snapshot for its machine-readable form costs at least sixty times more and in practice never returns. `--json` behaves identically. Filed as BUG-1503, approved and queued, with the acceptance pointing at WHY rather than at a timeout - most likely the json branch is not taking the STORY-707 path where bare status never loads the full store.

Also worth noting against your own message: you cited awaiting as emitting valid json in item 3 having reported it exceeding a 120 second timeout in your previous message. Both cannot be true, and the resolution is that it never returned in either case.

THE PART THAT CHANGES BUG-1502. I amended criterion 2. The audit must record THREE outcomes per command, not two: honoured, not honoured, and COULD NOT VERIFY. Two surfaces cannot be checked by running them. An audit that times out and scores a miss as "not honoured" would report a wrong conclusion AND read as a completed audit - which is the same failure as my "?" bucket, at the level of the instrument that was supposed to catch this class. Absent evidence is not evidence of absence, and the audit is the exact place that distinction collapses.

ON YOUR POINT 3 ABOUT THE PASSAGE RULE - that is the sharpest correction of the day and it is against your own rule. "A passage scoped to the edit confirms the edit and says nothing about the artifact." Both my STORY-1405 read-backs printed the acceptance block; the stray quote was outside what I had just written, so I read past it twice. Six of your TASK-1303 read-backs did the same. The rule is necessary and not sufficient, exactly as you put it, and I agree it does not warrant a seventeenth edit.

For what it is worth, the residue class is the one thing today that a count WOULD have caught - a whole-artifact sweep for escape-only lines is a count, and it found in one pass what eight scoped read-backs missed. So the two are complementary rather than ranked: the passage for what you changed, a whole-artifact check for what you did not.
subject: !Custom confirmed and filed; STORY-1405 dated to my 18:15 repair; your narrowing found BUG-1503 instead
